gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC gives its tall lowercase generous counters, with curves that open outward instead of curling in. And Quilon ebbs and flows just enough to give the text a confident lead.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Editorial punch comes from Quilon, whose thin strokes run about half the weight of its thick ones. Noto Sans Telugu handles the humbler work, with a high-set midline and counters that stay connected to the outside.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall lowercase bodies that look bold, plus spacious gaps where its curves end. But Quilon does its best work up top, where even its thinnest curves keep real weight.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Soft inflated bowls below a headline with a gentle pulse. Noto Sans Tifinagh keeps its rounded letters open and inviting, so reading flows along easily, while Quilon adds modest stroke modulation up top.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai sets words as solid blocks, not skylines. What stands out is how Quilon grades its weight along each rounded stroke, lending the sans-serif text room to breathe.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Fuller stems, slimmer links: Quilon moves with a soft cadence. Noto Sans Vithkuqi opens the throats of a, c, e, and s and barely steps from capital to lowercase, giving the pair a clean modern ease.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-questrial: Questrial cuts every stroke at a single weight, a flat, stencil-cut look with a tall band of letters. Quilon earns its keep big and short, where its modest thick-thin contrast shows.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sarpanch: Sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier thick ones: that's Quilon. Sarpanch follows with a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e and a compact gap to the ascender line, approachable and contemporary.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sulphur-point: Professional in tone, Sulphur Point draws a marker-like line with bulky lowercase and distinct open gaps. But Quilon lets its light strokes recede only slightly, so the two feel like cousins, one editorial, one rounded.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-vend-sans: A quiet ebb and flow of stroke weight gives Quilon its voice. Vend Sans, drawn with a ruler-constant line and an x-height that fills the line, lets Quilon do its best work big and short.
